item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Seriously. It's a pretty good example of how unrestricted test logs can generate some legitimately interesting (or even funny) results, but are pretty much guaranteed to run the joke into the ground.

Especially, the right way and the wrong way to do pop culture referencing. On one hand, it takes three increasingly explicit tries to get "Michael Myers, the horror movie villain/monster" right, and the preceding tries are humorous in a way that's still consistent with how the machine works. And then you get others, like the Undertale/Fortnite logs, which are basically "Haha, see, it's that game!"

item.content:encoded:
Thanks!

A tricky part was that the Ukrainian meaning, "cat", was very definitely used before. So I discussed it with my son, who originally introduced me to SCP (yes, this happens, parents get on the site), and he suggested adding an adjective. I took the most stereotypical Ukrainian adjective.

I want to add another experiment when a character is asked to say "kit" while not knowing any language where it is a word; a meaning from a rare language will be used. My problem is finding out whether "kit" is actually a word in Arabic. An Arabic speaker who speaks no European language is reasonably easy to write in (and will probably show up in the Romson story anyway).

On the other hand, while Finnish has no "kit", it's just unrealistic to have a Finn who does not speak English be anywhere near Sector-25, and this applies to any European language.

item.title: New Test Ideas
item.content:encoded:
I have an idea that basically recreates the bad endings of Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

Player: Guest Junior Technical Writer Bradley
Statement: Galeem.
Result: Several bolts of solid light emerged from one end of SCP-1459 and haphazardly impaled SCP-1459-1, leaving it stunned in pain and struggling to stand, but not terminated. Moments later, SCP-1459 was filled with a light that rapidly grew in intensity, visibly disintegrating the body of SCP-1459-1; within roughly 4 seconds, the light within the chamber was far too bright for any activity to be observed, as anyone who looked at it would be temporarily blinded and any camera viewing it would have its footage or photos be completely whited out. The light faded after 1 minute, leaving absolutely no trace of SCP-1459-1 within the chamber, not even blood or viscera; it is likely that it was reduced to its constituent atoms and vaporized. The dispensed cookie was pure white, and SCP-1459 was unusually silent as the cookie was dispensed.
Notes: AUGH!!! MY EYES, THEY BURN!!! This was a terrible idea!!! -GJTW Bradley

Player: Guest Junior Technical Writer Bradley
Statement: Dharkon.
Result: The light within SCP-1459 dimmed as though absorbed by a mysterious force, and SCP-1459-1's legs were impaled and pulled apart by several dark tentacles that emerged from the sides of the chamber, causing it to cry out in pain. Moments later, several more tentacles emerged from the bottom of the chamber and impaled SCP-1459-1's body, lifting it up into the air, with a couple of tentacles impaling its brain and chest; SCP-1459-1 did not cry out in pain despite bleeding profusely, and was likely terminated instantly by the destruction of its brain and heart. The tentacles began lifting SCP-1459-1's corpse into the hatch at the top of SCP-1459-1, while the light within the chamber continued to dim; within 4 seconds, the chamber's interior was so dark that even low-light viewing technology showed it as a solid black space, though thermal imagery showed the corpse of SCP-1459-1 vanishing into the space at the top of SCP-1459 and the usual array of robotic arms emerging from the hatch and cleaning the chamber as normal. The chamber of SCP-1459 returned to normal lighting after 1 minute, by which time the corpse of SCP-1459-1 had been fully disposed of and the chamber had been completely cleaned. The dispensed cookie was pitch-black as though it had been thoroughly burned; chemical analysis indicated that the cookie was not actually burnt. SCP-1459 was silent while dispensing the cookie.
